💬 Feedback & Suggestions Welcome

Your feedback is incredibly valuable!

Let me know in the comments what you think about:

  • Spawn rates (too high? too rare?)
  • Card balance or theme ideas
  • Suggestions for new cards, features or tweaks

I’m open to all ideas — this mod is community-driven at heart!

🎚️ Adjusting Card Spawn Rates

Cards still too common—or not common enough?

You now have two simple levers in config/mod_config.json:

  1. Global multiplier – card_weight_multiplier
    • 0 = no cards at all
    • 0.5= low
    • 1 = normal (≈ 9 % per loot roll) ← default
    • 2 = medium (≈ 18 %)
    • 3 = high (≈ 27 %)Raise or lower this single number to scale every rarity up or down at once.
  2. Per-rarity share – six numbers that must add up to 1.0Fine-tune how the total card budget is divided among rarities.

Tip: Start by adjusting the multiplier; touch the rarity fractions only if you want a different curve (e.g., more Rares, fewer Commons).

Containers:

comments.body_html:
Since v1.1.0 the math has changed—you no longer have to recalculate every rarity value.

  • Use card_weight_multiplier in mod_config.json to scale the entire drop rate:

    • 0 = no cards, 1 ≈ 9 % per loot roll (default, previously was 50% !), 2 ≈ 18 %, etc.

  • Leave the six rarity numbers adding up to 1.0; they only control how that global pool is split between Common, Uncommon, Rare, etc.

So, to cut overall drops to one-third, just set:

“card_weight_multiplier”: 0.3333 // or simply 0 (none), 0.5 (low), 1 (normal), 2 (medium), 3 (high) But should be fine keeping “1” now.

No need to touch the per-rarity values unless you also want to change the curve. Hope that makes tuning a lot easier!

comments.author: Chazut
comments.body_html:
Thanks a lot for the thoughtful feedback — really appreciate it!

You’re totally right — loot balance is one of the hardest things to get right, especially for a collectible mod like this.

If the spawn rate is too low, people comment “I can’t find any cards!” — too high, and it feels like they’re everywhere, drowning out valuable loot. It’s a tough middle ground to find.

What makes it even trickier is that everyone runs different mods. For example, early on I had a spawn rate I thought was fair… but I was using “Late to the Party,” which removes loot over time, so things felt balanced. Others have mods that boost loot, or change how containers are filled — so the card weight can end up being too strong or too weak depending on loadout.

That’s exactly why I made the spawn system configurable, so each player can tweak it to match their setup. The default values aim to work for most people, but I rely on your feedback to adjust those defaults over time, and this kind of report is super valuable. 🙏

Lowering the multiplier to 0.05 is a huge drop — sounds like it hits a sweet spot for your setup, which is awesome to hear. Based on this and similar feedback, I’ll likely reduce the default multiplier again in the next update.

Thanks again, and happy looting 😉!

comments.author: Chazut
comments.body_html:
Hey,

Every TTC item (cards, binders, boosters, crates) explicitly declares a Handbook price, with safety fallbacks. So TTC items shouldn’t be missing handbook entries on their own.

The crash you’re seeing (FenceBaseAssortGenerator –> HandbookHelper.GetTemplatePrice returning null) usually means another mod is trying to push an item into Fence’s pool before its handbook entry is registered. Raid Overhaul can be a suspect if it touches trader assorts and load order can matter there.

Can you try removing Raid Overhaul instead of TTC and see if the crash goes away? That should tell us right away if it’s a load order conflict.
